data.narrative:
Layup Parts is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Zack Eakin that has raised $2M+. The valuation universe comprises one public comparable (277810.KQ) and eight private peers in the robotics and manufacturing sector, including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI.

Standard triangulation methods yield limited conclusions. Stage-progression analysis proved inapplicable: the method generated an implied $105M valuation based on a $42M funding-tracker proxy, which exceeds the company's actual total raised by more than 20x and fails basic sanity checks. Peer-median analysis was also not applicable due to insufficient narrow comparables—while ten same-sector peers exist, filtering to same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-valuation-tier cohorts yielded fewer than three datapoints. A broader all-sector median would sacrifice analytical precision.

Given these constraints, a valuation range cannot be reliably established from the available data. The core uncertainty is the thinness of the comparable set at the seed stage within this specialized sector. Forward analysis would require either: expanding the comparable universe to include earlier-stage robotics companies or adjacent hardware automation plays, obtaining cleaned funding and revenue data from existing private peers to establish meaningful multiples, or establishing transaction or primary-round pricing data for Layup Parts itself. Without additional datapoints, the company's fair value remains indeterminate from a peer-triangulation perspective.
